item.title: Fast Computation of the Kippenhahn Hypersurface of a Joint Numerical Range
item.description: arXiv:2611.14543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a fast modular interpolation method for computing the hypersurface components of algebraic Kippenhahn varieties over number fields. Starting from Hermitian matrices, we factor their determinantal polynomial and use Katz's test to identify the factors whose duals are hypersurfaces. For each such factor, we sample smooth points over finite fields and compute their tangent hyperplanes. These give points on the dual hypersurface, from which we interpolate its defining equation. For number-field coefficients, we use primes at which the defining polynomial of the field factors completely into distinct linear factors. Interpolation across all its roots recovers the residues of the coefficients in a fixed number-field basis. Chinese remaindering and rational reconstruction then recover an equation over the original number field from the computations at different primes. An exact polynomial divisibility test and an irreducibility check certify each reconstructed equation. Four determinantal quartics arising from matrix examples in the literature yield certified dual surfaces of degrees $12$, $18$, $24$ and $34$. We give implementations in Magma and Singular and compare their running times with Gr\"obner basis elimination.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Rito

item.title: Involutive Duality of Lie Operators in the Extended Alpha Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.14547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates the involutive, adjoint, and spectral structures arising in the extended Alpha Group. Starting from the four-dimensional Alpha Group transformation matrix, whose angular depen- dence is governed by coupled tan {\theta} and cot {\theta} modes, an iterative commutator procedure generates a sixteen-dimensional real Lie algebra. Within this algebra, the operators B5 and B6 are identified as structurally distinguished elements and analyzed through their adjoint actions. The operator B6 is veri- fied to be involutive and induces an 8 + 8 decomposition of the Lie algebra, while the adjoint action of B5 defines an eight-dimensional invariant mixed sector through a polynomial kernel. The restricted adjoint operators preserve this sector, and their coupled action generates an idempotent operator Q, satisfying Q2 = Q, revealing an invariant projective structure. The spectral analysis further identifies characteristic- polynomial factorizations associated with B5 , B6 , and their compositions, including golden-ratio relations among distinct generators of the extended algebra. These results establish structural connections between the original modal representation, Lie-algebraic involution, adjoint dynamics, projective organization, and the spectral structure of the extended Alpha Group.
item.dc:creator: Cleber Souza Correa, Thiago Braido Nogueira de Melo

item.title: Another Multivector Inverse Algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2611.14549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A numerical algorithm is described for computing the inverse of a non-singular multivector across dimensions. The method wraps a reversion-like product around a Faddeev--LeVerrier--Souriau (FLS) polynomial core. While FLS provides dimensional extensibility, the wrapper reduces the polynomial order of the FLS method, and introduces a sparse multivector which can be further exploited. The construction and essential properties of the initial involution are explained. For dimensions 4--7, the optimized inverse requires fewer real multiplications than a same-dimension multivector product. Dimensions 8--11 follow easily on common hardware with similar efficiency. For dimensions 12--15, higher-precision arithmetic demonstrates the generality of the algorithm when the arithmetic can support it. Performance on common hardware is reported. Directions are included for obtaining a Python package with examples for numerical computation in Clifford algebra, supporting arbitrary signatures including degenerate cases.
item.dc:creator: David Arthur Jones

item.title: Finite bases for matrix semirings: transfer theorems and nilpotent counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2611.14551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We first show that the nonfinitely based six-element ai-semiring $SR_6$ has finitely based full matrix semirings for every $n\ge2$, with a four-identity basis relative to the ai-semiring axioms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first known example of this phenomenon. We then construct a countably infinite flat ai-semiring $P$ whose scalar and two-by-two matrix varieties are nonfinitely based, whereas its matrix varieties in sizes $n\ge3$ admit a five-identity relative basis. For both examples, the intervals from the scalar variety to each matrix variety of size at least two have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Finally, we establish transfer results for stronger forms of nonfinite basability and a finite-basis dichotomy for matrix semirings of size at least two over scalars with a genuine zero generating a locally finite variety: finite basability in the multiplicatively nilpotent case, and inherent nonfinite basability otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Jun Jiao

item.title: Relative divisors and intersections of noncommutative rational localizations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The simple constituents of monic pencils determine singularity support in a free skew field. For a pencil inverse algebra that is a free ideal ring, the multiplicities of the nonbase constituents compute the scalar-regular part of Cohn's matrix divisor theory. For independent generic invertible matrices of size at least two, every entry of a nonidentity free-group word is an atom with one relative singularity component. In rank two, opposite pivots give the exact identifications among these components. Intersections of word-entry localizations are then given by intersections of their label sets. An irreducible pencil of dimension six represents a commutator entry. For an algebra finitely generated over the free polynomial algebra at a common regular scalar point, the residual closure is a finite pencil inverse algebra determined by the generators' common domain. Every nonzero inverse-adjoining defect is infinite-dimensional. We compute how free-group quotients change intersections and give additive formulas for general quotient and tensor intersections. We prove Berenstein--Retakh's polygon conjecture using $n-2$ charts for $n\geq4$. For an unpunctured M\"obius strip with $n\geq2$ boundary marks, the upper-algebra equality follows from $n+1$ charts. For the once-marked strip, the allowed algebra is strictly smaller than its residual hull, which equals the full chart.
item.dc:creator: Mahesh Ramani

item.title: Spectra of gcd-graphs over a matrix ring
item.description: arXiv:2611.15026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note, we calculate the spectra of gcd-graphs defined over a matrix ring. Using character sums, we show that this calculation can be reduced to certain counting problems. In particular, when the underlying ring is a matrix ring with coefficients in a finite field, we calculate these spectra explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Tung T. Nguyen

item.title: Dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Artin--Schelter Gorenstein and Artin--Schelter regular properties descend from a graded Ore extension to its coefficient algebra, for every twisting automorphism and every skew derivation. We then determine the dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions for all gradings compatible with the Ore structure. They are exactly the semidirect products of a dual reflection group of the coefficient algebra by the cyclic group generated by the degree of the new variable, meeting it trivially, and a nonzero skew derivation never contributes a new degree. For iterated Ore extensions we characterize the dual reflection groups by an order formula analogous to the theorem of Shephard, Todd and Chevalley, and we prove the binomial conjecture of Buzaglo and Rogalski for these algebras. We show that their covariant rings are complete intersections of growth type, whose Ext-algebras grow like a polynomial ring in as many variables as there are generators of nontrivial degree. This answers a question of Kirkman, Kuzmanovich and Zhang for these algebras. Finally, we describe the smash product as a Cayley quiver with relations, factor its matrix Hilbert series, and show that the extension becomes Hopf--Galois once the Jacobian is inverted.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Ait Mohamed, Asmae El-Baz

item.title: Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.16086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.
item.dc:creator: A. N. Abyzov, O. V. Lyubimtsev, A. A. Tuganbaev

item.title: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.16165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: G\'abor Cz\'edli introduced congruence density and investigated how it changes under sublattice extensions. We prove that density cannot increase: if $S$ is a sublattice of a finite lattice $L$, then $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. We also determine when equality holds: $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ precisely when every element of $L\setminus S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of Cz\'edli and Szab\'o relating quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding results for quasiorder density.
item.dc:creator: George Gr\"atzer

item.title: Uniqueness of addition in Schr\"odinger algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.16812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain a criterion for the uniqueness of addition in Schr\"odinger Lie algebras, applicable to both bijections and injections. This allows us to construct the first example of a Lie algebra with unique addition and a non-trivial center over a field of characteristic zero. Furthermore, a necessary and sufficient condition is established for the Schr\"odinger algebras to have bracket width one.
item.dc:creator: Gennadiy Sosnov

item.title: Rings with unequal $\operatorname{slip-spli}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a unital associative ring $R$, let $\operatorname{silp}(R)$ be the supremum of the injective dimensions of all projective right $R$-modules, and let $\operatorname{spli}(R)$ be the supremum of the projective dimensions of all injective right $R$-modules. We construct an explicit non-Noetherian unital algebra \[R=k1\oplus \frac{k(0\longrightarrow1\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow\cdots)} {\langle\text{all paths of length }2\rangle}\] over any field and prove that $\operatorname{silp}(R)=1$ and $\operatorname{spli}(R)=\infty. $ The algebra is the unitization of the non-unital path algebra of the one-sided infinite ray modulo paths of length two. The example answers the question whether $\operatorname{silp=spli}$ raised by Gedrich and Gruenberg.
item.dc:creator: Xuyang Chen, Honghui Ding

item.title: What the occupation law of a finite Markov chain determines: time reversal and principal minors
item.description: arXiv:2611.14587v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: What does the occupation law of a finite Markov chain determine about its generator $Q$? From the stationary start, the law of the occupation times at one time determines $Q$ exactly up to time reversal and reversals of memoryless blocks, the sets of states that are all left at one rate with one landing law and are entered in proportion to the stationary law. These reversals commute and give exactly $2^k$ generators, with $k$ read off a tree of memoryless blocks. This leaves only time reversal when $Q$ has no rank-one cut, when there are at most 4 states, and generically. The law at one time determines the law at every time, and a generic start determines $Q$. A renewal block is a set of states that is left at the same rates from each of its states, is entered with one law, and is charged by the start in proportion to that law. From every start the law determines $Q$ exactly up to lumped reversals, which lump disjoint renewal blocks to single states and reverse a memoryless block of the lumped chain. We also find every start that hides time reversal. At the scale of large deviations, the functional of Donsker and Varadhan determines exactly the principal minors of $-Q$.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Pemmasani

item.title: Twisted algebras of invariant formal power series over monoids
item.description: arXiv:2611.14667v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a general monoid-theoretic framework to construct and study graded and color Hopf algebras of formal power series of bounded degree invariant under group actions. Rather than working with external alphabets of commuting, noncommuting, or anti-commuting variables, we start from an abstract monoid $M$ equipped with a $2$-cocycle twisting $\tau:M\times M\to \mathbb{K}$, which is allowed to vanish, a bigrading over a commutative monoid $\mathcal{G}\times\mathbb{N}$ endowed with a bicharacter $\phi$, and a group $G$ acting on $M$ via a bigraded action $\rho$ that is quasi-multiplicative with respect to $\tau$, coupled with a $1$-cocycle weight function $\omega:G\times M\to\mathbb{K}^\times$. By formulating local finiteness, gradings, quasi-multiplicativity, and ideals relative to the non-vanishing of $\tau$, we prove that the invariant space $\mathbb{K}\langle\kern-0.2em\langle M\rangle\kern-0.2em\rangle^G$ forms a well-defined bigraded subalgebra of bounded-degree formal power series with a canonical monomial basis indexed by $\omega$-admissible orbits. Furthermore, we establish four functorial constructions: embeddings into larger invariant algebras via restricted actions, color tensor product decompositions for direct products and diagonal actions, connected color Hopf algebra structures induced by internal monoid duplication, and quotient color Hopf algebras governed by invariant-retraction pairs with an explicit description of their kernel bi-ideals. As applications, we uniformly recover and extend the classical and twisted Hopf algebras of symmetric and quasisymmetric functions in commuting and noncommuting variables, MacMahon symmetric functions, the full square of symmetric and quasisymmetric Hopf algebras in superspace, symmetric and quasisymmetric functions in partially commutative variables, and signed-symmetric functions associated with the hyperoctahedral group.
item.dc:creator: Diego Arcis, Camilo Gonz\'alez, Sebasti\'an M\'arquez

item.title: Bipartite Matchings, Matrix Permanents, and Zeon Power Series
item.description: arXiv:2611.14802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Perfect matchings of a bipartite graph are counted by the permanent of the graph's biadjacency matrix, and permanents of sequences of structured biadjacency matrices lead to integer sequences. We consider a number of such sequences and illustrate how zeon-algebraic representations of bipartite graphs lead to recursively defined zeon sequences. Then, using formal power series methods, we show that the ``$\Omega$-exponentials'' of these zeon sequences reveal numbers of perfect matchings in the graphs.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Waqar Ul Hassan, G. Stacey Staples

item.title: Hopf algebras of leaf-graded forests
item.description: arXiv:2611.14812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Xiao

item.title: Automating the Derivation of Advanced Algorithms in Numerical Linear Algebra using Associative Algebras with Involution
item.description: arXiv:2611.14831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard algorithms of numerical linear algebra use their scalars through seven operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the adjoint, the $*$-square root and $(i,j)$ indexing. This thesis overloads these operations, as automatic differentiation overloads arithmetic, allowing scalars in associative algebras with involution. Many of the resulting decompositions and algorithms reduce to Hermitian eigendecomposition over these $*$-algebras. The decompositions are organised by doubly-signed quivers, whose vertices record real, complex or quaternionic scalars and the action of the involution. We prove an analogue of Gabriel's theorem: every finite-dimensional real $*$-algebra is a matrix algebra, with sizes and signs, over a quotient of its quiver's path $*$-algebra. Spectral theorems, the singular value decomposition, Takagi factorisation, Sylvester's law of inertia and the real Jordan form arise as unitary similarity problems for Hermitian matrices. Division and square roots take place in a completed localisation which inverts the arrows. For the singular value decomposition, Householder tridiagonalisation becomes Golub--Kahan bidiagonalisation. Over split-complex numbers, the QR algorithm becomes Rutishauser's LR algorithm, two steps at a time, and Cholesky factorisation becomes Doolittle's LU factorisation. These identifications require suitable $*$-square roots and hold whenever the steps are defined. Infinitesimals make limits of algorithms exact computations: Gram--Schmidt yields the Bruhat decomposition, and Gaussian elimination with pivots chosen by orders of magnitude yields Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm in leading terms. A Python library implements the seven operations and algorithms. An appendix visualises the QR algorithm on $2\times2$ real matrices.
item.dc:creator: Ran Gutin

item.title: Lax Centers and Monoidal Functors for Comodule Categories Associated with Acyclic Quivers
item.description: arXiv:2611.15496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the monoidal category of finite-dimensional right comodules over the path algebra $\Bbbk Q$ of a finite acyclic quiver $Q$, equipped with the weak bialgebra structure in which every path is grouplike. We prove that the lax center of this category is monoidally equivalent to $\operatorname{Rep}^{\mathrm{fd}}_{\Bbbk}(Q)$, the category of finite-dimensional representations of $Q$. We also classify all $\Bbbk$-linear strong monoidal functors between any two such comodule categories, and all monoidal natural transformations between them. For the right adjoint of such a functor, we determine when the left or right projection formula holds. When both projection formulas hold, this adjoint will induce a functor between the lax centers, and we describe the induced functor explicitly on quiver representations.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Zhao, Jingheng Zhou

item.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
item.description: arXiv:2611.15540v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: Categorical orbifold theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.15630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the orbifold theory for condensable algebras in fusion categories $\mathcal{C}$. We prove that the algebra automorphism group of a condensable algebra $A$ is finite and explicitly characterize its elements in terms of the fusion action and indecomposable $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$-bimodule decomposition of $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. We further show that a finite group action on $A$ gives rise to a group extension of the category $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$ in $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. Conversely, every such group extension arises from a finite group of algebra automorphisms of $A$. Finally, we also construct a canonical maximal group extension of $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$, thereby providing a categorical framework for the classical correspondence among finite group actions, fixed-point algebras, and twisted modules.
item.dc:creator: Chongying Dong, Siu-Hung Ng, Li Ren, Feng Xu

item.title: Point symmetries and Lie reductions of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.15833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the point symmetry pseudogroup of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation using both the direct and the algebraic methods. We also revisit the classical Lie symmetry analysis of this model in detail, concentrating on hidden infinitesimal and hidden point symmetries. Additionally, we re-examine the symmetry properties of each codimension-one reduced model and determine their point symmetry pseudogroups.
item.dc:creator: Yevhenii Yu. Chapovskyi, Serhii D. Koval

item.title: Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.16024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius. This settles a question of Hernandez--Walton--Yadav and unifies a wealth of results in the literature. We conclude with applications to topological quantum field theories and Poincar\'e duality algebras.
item.dc:creator: Pablo S. Ocal

item.title: Matrix Waring Problem in finite fields with coefficients from $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer and $p$ be an odd prime such that $\gcd(p-1,k)=1$. For sufficiently large primes $p$, we show that the equation $AX^k+BY^k=C$ has solutions $X,Y \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $A$ and $B$ are fixed matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and $C$ is a fixed matrix in $\mathrm{M}(2,\mathbb{F}_p).$ Our proof relies on Fourier analysis over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p).$
item.dc:creator: Sutirtha Datta, Sourav Ghosh, Aniruddha Maji, Antara Manik

item.title: Free G\"odel algebras over G\"odel hoops
item.description: arXiv:2611.16695v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an explicit description of the left adjoint $F$ of the forgetful functor $U\colon\mathsf{GAlg}\to\mathsf{GHoops}$ from G\"odel algebras to G\"odel hoops. If $H$ is a G\"odel hoop with a least element $m$, then $F(H)$ is the direct product of the G\"odel algebra obtained by adjoining a new bottom element to $H$ and of $H$ itself, regarded as a G\"odel algebra with bottom element $m$. For an arbitrary G\"odel hoop $H$, we glue these products along the principal filters of $H$, and we describe the operations of $F(H)$, the action of $F$ on homomorphisms and the unit of the adjunction. As an application, we show that the unit of the adjunction $F\dashv U$ is not cartesian, and that the same holds for BL-algebras and basic hoops. Moreover, the semi-abelian categories of G\"odel hoops and of basic hoops are not equivalent to the slice categories of G\"odel algebras and of BL-algebras over their initial object. Thus, in contrast with the cases of Wajsberg hoops and of product hoops, the free-forgetful adjunctions between G\"odel algebras and G\"odel hoops, and between BL-algebras and basic hoops, do not give rise to ideally exact contexts.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Mancini

item.title: The Simplicial Cylinder DG Ring
item.description: arXiv:2602.11943v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Keller cylinder DG ring encodes homotopies between DG ring homomorphisms $f_0, f_1 : A \to B$. Recently we discovered the higher cylinder DG rings $Cyl_q(B)$, which assemble into the simplicial cylinder DG ring $Cyl(B)$. For $q=1$ this recovers Keller's original construction. The sets $SHom_q(A,B)$ of DG ring homomorphisms $A \to Cyl_q(B)$ form the simplicial Hom set $SHom(A,B)$. Our main result is that when $A$ is a semi-free DG ring, the simplicial set $SHom(A,B)$ is a Kan complex. We prove several results about the fundamental groupoid $SHom_{\leq 1}(A,B)$, including invariance under quasi-isomorphism $B' \to B$.
item.dc:creator: Amnon Yekutieli

item.title: Classification of Two-Dimensional Algebras and the Number of Non-isomorphic Two-Dimensional Algebras over a Finite Field
item.description: arXiv:2603.15148v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An updated classification of two-dimensional algebras over an arbitrary base field is provided, along with the number of non-isomorphic such algebras over a finite field.
item.dc:creator: U. Bekbaev

item.title: Implication semilattice of 990 quadratic quasigroup equational laws
item.description: arXiv:2603.29909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In his quest to exhibit a non-distributive lattice, Ernst Schr\"oder considered 135 years ago a list of 990 equational laws on quasigroups, a non-associative generalization of groups. The laws of interest are analogues of associativity, such as $(x // y) * z = (y // x) \backslash\backslash z$, built from the multiplication $*$ and right/left conjugate-division operations, with the same three distinct variables on both sides. I determine all 114 equivalence classes of their conjunctions, and all implications between them. This includes as a small corner the non-distributive lattice identified by Schr\"oder. Apart from 31 classes that are related to inverse properties (and weaker than total symmetry), and 3 that describe groups and their parastrophes, the remaining 80 are subject to the Four Quasigroups Theorem and quasigroups satisfying them are isotopes of Abelian groups. More than half of these describe (affine) modules over interesting rings.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Le Floch

item.title: Lie algebras with only inner derivations and applications to finite $p$-groups
item.description: arXiv:2605.04602v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper begins by studying Lie algebras of the form $\mathcal L=\mathcal S\ltimes\mathcal N$ with only inner derivations. We extend Sato's construction to infinite families of such Lie algebras and answer Carles's question by exhibiting a $19$-dimensional complete non-perfect Lie algebra with nilpotent radical. Applying our construction, we derive a family of finite $p$-groups $P$ with $|\Aut(G)|=|P|$ for any $p\geq7$. Moreover, we show that for arbitrarily small $\alpha>0$ and every prime $p\geq7$, there exists a finite $p$-group $P$ such that $|\Aut(P)|<\varphi(|P|)^\alpha$. This is a preliminary version of the manuscript, and some sections are still being revised.
item.dc:creator: Yunsong Gan, Bakhrom Omirov, Jie Ruan

item.title: Support $\tau$-tilting posets and Hochschild reconstruction for matrix centralizer algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.15460v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R$ be a field and $A$ the endomorphism algebra of a finite direct sum of cyclic modules over a finite-dimensional commutative local principal ideal $R$-algebra. An explicit central quotient identifies the support $\tau$-tilting poset of $A$ with the weak order on a symmetric group. The center of $A$, together with degree-zero Hochschild homology as a module over the center, recovers the truncated local algebra and the multiset of successive length gaps. Applied to centralizer matrix algebras, these results show that the support $\tau$-tilting poset determines exactly the multiset of distinct-exponent counts of the primary blocks, whereas the center--Hochschild pair recovers their local algebras and gap multisets. Combined with the known classification, this characterizes derived equivalence by isomorphism of these algebra--module pairs. We also establish Morita reconstruction results in the string and gentle classes.
item.dc:creator: Jiangsheng Hu, Yu-Zhe Liu, Tiwei Zhao

item.title: Counterexamples to the pure semisimplicity conjecture and Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(m)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.39883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum chains of division rings yield counterexamples to the pure semisimplicity conjecture and hereditary artinian rings of every Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(m)$ with $m \geq 4$. For a field element $q$ of multiplicative order $\ell \geq 2$, possibly infinite, the construction gives an extension $H \subseteq T$ with right dimension $2$ and left dimension $\ell$. If $\ell = \infty$, the associated triangular ring is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, the parameters $q = 2, 3, 4, \dots$ give pairwise Morita inequivalent counterexamples. If $\ell<\infty$, the ring is of finite representation type with Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(\ell+2)$, and the right dimension sequence of ${}_HT_T$ is periodic with period $(1, 2, \ldots, 2, 1, \ell)$, where $2$ occurs $\ell-1$ times. Every finite $\ell \geq 2$ is realized by choosing $q$ to be a primitive $\ell$-th root of unity.
item.dc:creator: Junpeng Ren

item.title: Linear structure graphs associated with commuting graphs of Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.10788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The commuting graph (CG) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero forgets the linear structure, and a non-trivial center creates redundant vertices. We introduce linear structure graphs (LSGs), whose vertices are the nonzero vectors of a vector space and whose edge set is stable under linear operations. Each vertex generates a finite ascending sequence of subspaces, which defines its LSG-height; this height governs connectivity. We characterize LSGs of height at most 1 and show that the CG of a Lie algebra with trivial center has height at most 1 if and only if the algebra is a commutative transitive Lie algebra (CTLA). The reduced commuting graph (RCG) restricts the CG to a complement of the center; it is well defined up to LSG-isomorphism, preserves the connectivity, diameter and number of components of the CG, and is compatible with direct sums. Finally, we characterize almost abelian Lie algebras (AALAs) by their RCGs.
item.dc:creator: Vu A. Le, Hoa Q. Duong, Tuan A. Nguyen

item.title: Automatic Continuity for projective clone homomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.14490v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that every projective clone homomorphism from a closed function clone containing the automorphism group of a countable homogeneous Ramsey structure $\Delta$ in a finite relational language is uniformly continuous. This answers, for such structures, open questions previously raised by Barto, Bodirsky, Marimon, Pongr\'acz, and the second author in several papers (Bodirsky, Pinsker, Pongr\'acz, J. Symb. Log. 2021; Barto, Pinsker, SIAM J. Comput. 2020; Marimon, Pinsker, arXiv:2512.01086). Consequently, the polymorphism clone of a first-order reduct $\Gamma$ of $\Delta$ admits a projective clone homomorphism if and only if $\Gamma$ primitively positively interprets all finite structures; in other words, this ability of $\Gamma$ is characterised by the absence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, a purely algebraic condition.
item.dc:creator: Leopold Karl, Michael Pinsker

item.title: Classification of the d-representation-finite symmetric k-algebras of finite representation type
item.description: arXiv:2103.15380v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a complete classification of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric Nakayama algebras and of all $d$-representation-finite trivial extensions of path algebras of quivers, over an arbitrary field. As a consequence we get a classification, up to Morita equivalence, of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric algebras of finite representation type over an algebraically closed field.
item.dc:creator: Erik Darp\"o, Tor Kringeland

item.title: Crystal Structure of Upper Cluster Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2309.08326v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct upper seminormal crystals on the $\mu$-supported tropical points of skew-symmetric cluster algebras from their exchange matrices. A generic potential provides an additive categorification in which boundary representations determine the Cartan matrices and generic ranks describe the crystal operators. Under frozen-Jacobi-finiteness and reachability, the raising operators lift to locally nilpotent derivations of the upper cluster algebra. For $\tau$-exact boundary pairs, these derivations give integrable actions of derived Kac--Moody algebras in characteristic zero. In particular, the associated Cartan matrices are positive semidefinite. When the generic characters form a basis, this basis is BK-biperfect and the $\tau$-exact crystals are normal. We also construct algebraic Tits actions and describe compatibly pointed biperfect bases through a coefficient graph. The theory is illustrated by classical and new examples.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Zero-divisor algebras of graph functions: quantum caging, entangling routing and stochastic first-passage exclusion
item.description: arXiv:2311.11978v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show how algebraic constraints on weighted graphs yield exact localization and controlled transport in quantum and stochastic systems. Antisymmetrizing a noncommutative, nonassociative product of vertex functions defines a Lie bracket. For a specified Lie cobracket over commutative rings without nonzero $2$-torsion, compatibility holds if and only if products of distinct incident edge weights vanish. When the coefficient ring is a finite product of integral domains, the edges with nonzero weights in each component of the ring form a matching. These matchings are determined by the edge weights and need not coincide across the components. These matchings yield exact two-vertex caging in fixed quantum channels; separately specified channel-selective controls enable coherent routing and path--internal-state entanglement. For matching-supported stochastic jump rates, they enforce first-passage exclusion, while prescribed internal-state switching opens inaccessible paths and yields a singular weak-switching escape limit. The bracket--cobracket factorization identifies a common edge operator underlying quantum kinetic Hamiltonians and Markov generators, subject to distinct sign and positivity conditions. The algebra fixes the channel structure; controlled motion requires additional dynamical operations.
item.dc:creator: F\"ul\"op Bazs\'o

item.title: Applications of reduced and coreduced modules III: Derived torsion and completion over polynomial extensions
item.description: arXiv:2502.02937v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study when degree-zero identities for reduced and coreduced modules extend to ambient derived torsion and completion. For a non-idempotent ideal $I$ in an explicit polynomial ring, we construct a module $M$ that is simultaneously $I$-reduced and $I$-coreduced and satisfies $\Gamma_I(M)=\Lambda_I(M)=0$ but $H_I^2(M)\ne0$. The module is a union of finite reduced and coreduced submodules whose positive derived torsion vanishes. The supporting ideal has unrestricted torsion dimension two, whereas the dimension on each bounded-nilpotence quotient category is one. The calculations use compatible cone resolutions for $R=S[t]$ and $I=JS[t]+(t)$, where $J^2=J$. These give paired Ext--Tor formulas for coefficients annihilated by a fixed power of $t$. For arbitrary coefficients, an explicit mapping-fiber model realizes the standard derived-composition comparison sequence and identifies the obstruction to extending the bounded formula. Coordinate calculations for countably idempotent-generated ideals supply the computational foundation, and a valuation-domain example gives nonzero first derived completion on a cyclic reduced and coreduced coefficient.
item.dc:creator: David Ssevviiri

item.title: Quivers with Polynomial Identities
item.description: arXiv:2508.00662v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a topological characterization of quivers whose path algebra satisfies a polynomial identity. This class includes the oriented cycle and acyclic quivers and, in the latter case, we describe the associated T-ideal. We introduce a generalization of Arnold's A-graded algebras, which we call locally A-graded algebras, and prove that they are also PI. We give an example of a quiver algebra satisfying a polynomial identity, even if the path algebra of the quiver does not.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Cerulli Irelli, Javier De Loera Ch\'avez, Elena Pascucci

item.title: Higher representation infinite algebras and toric Fano stacks of Picard number one or two
item.description: arXiv:2511.02641v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the existence of and classify basic $d$-tilting bundles consisting of line bundles on d-dimensional smooth toric Fano stacks of Picard number one or two. A $d$-tilting bundle is a tilting bundle whose endomorphism algebra has global dimension at most $d$. The classification is motivated by dimer models, where internal perfect matchings give rise to $2$-representation infinite algebras. The algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$ introduced by Herschend, Iyama and Oppermann are higher-dimensional analogues in the simplex case. The same principle leads to a new class of algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$. Upper sets provide a common framework for tilting bundles, toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs), and cuts of higher-dimensional dimer-type quivers. In the Picard-number-one case, the bundles are in bijection with non-trivial upper sets in the Picard group, and their endomorphism algebras are precisely $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$. In the Picard-number-two case, a first upper set determines the ambient toric NCCR, and a second selects an internal cut of its quiver. This gives a complete classification of such $d$-tilting bundles and realizes their endomorphism algebras precisely as $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$. The resulting geometric models give a combinatorial description of $d$-APR tilting modules and show that both classes of algebras are closed under $d$-APR tilts.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: Induced quadratic structures of operated algebras with applications to multi-Novikov algebras
item.description: arXiv:2603.19553v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate binary-quadratic induced structures for unary--binary operads by taking the arity-three part of the kernel of the substitution map for chosen induced binary operations. Our purpose is to identify all universal relations in this quadratic class; we make no claim that they generate the full kernel in every arity. For commutative associative algebras equipped with families of derivations, we determine these quadratic relations explicitly. In the noncommuting-derivation case they give the noncommuting multi-Novikov operad; imposing commutation of the derivations yields exactly the additional relations of the multi-Novikov operad. The one-derivation specialization recovers the usual Novikov operad. The calculations are self-contained at arity three and display how operator identities control induced binary-quadratic structures.
item.dc:creator: Li Guo, Xiaoyan Wang, Huhu Zhang
